claims.text: Outside Nb-Ta-dominant systems, superconducting transition temperature is governed primarily by valence electron count.
Replacing a constituent with an element of higher valence electron count increases the alloy's overall electron count.
Increasing valence electron count shifts the Fermi level into a region of enhanced electronic density of states.
An elevated density of states at the Fermi level strengthens electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling increases or otherwise tunes the superconducting transition temperature.
A Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr-Hf high-entropy alloy can serve as a single-phase BCC starting material.
The proposed Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr-Hf alloy family exhibits BCS-type superconductivity.
The starting alloy must contain at least five elements, each at no less than 5 atomic percent.
The higher-valence substitution can modify the density of states without introducing significant additional disorder.
Keeping crystal structure, mixing entropy, processing, and thermal treatment comparable isolates electron count as the manipulated variable.
The transition temperature will change systematically with the size of the electron-count increment.
The modified alloy will have a higher density of states at the Fermi level than the baseline alloy.
The electronic specific-heat coefficient can be used to estimate the density of states at the Fermi level.
A relevant high-entropy-alloy baseline can have a superconducting transition temperature on the order of 7 K.
Specific-heat behavior can establish that superconductivity is a bulk effect rather than merely a resistive transition.
The proposed mechanism is applicable only while the alloy remains a single-phase BCC solid solution without substantial additional disorder.
Valence electron count alone may not quantitatively predict transition temperature because disorder, effective valence, and detailed electronic structure can also matter.
Failure to observe a reproducible electron-count–density-of-states–Tc correlation beyond experimental uncertainty would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is framed as applying outside Nb-Ta-dominant or best-studied systems, but the proposed starting material and baseline are the well-studied Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr-Hf family represented by the cited evidence.
